title: Seamless
haiku:
The last Arctic shaft
goes quiet; the miners climb
out into cold light
headline: Norway has closed its last coal mine, ending a way of life in the Arctic.

title: Catchment
haiku:
A sieve for shadows—
seven hundred thousand screened:
catch it while it's small
headline: The NHS has launched the world's largest trial of AI-assisted breast cancer screening, enrolling hundreds of thousands of women to test whether machines can help catch tumors earlier.

title: Unsentenced
haiku:
The ledger goes blank
where their names were crimes; I watch
the ink let them go
headline: Britain is wiping the criminal records of women who were convicted of abortion offences.

title: Percolation
haiku:
Groundwater rises
under the statehouse floors — slow,
the aquifer votes
headline: Midterm voters flipped enough state legislatures to end years of Republican dominance in statehouses across the country.

title: Buoyancy
haiku:
A ship on her side
the whole manifest counted
not a miracle
headline: Every passenger and crew member was rescued after a cruise ship collided with a tanker and rolled onto its side on the Mississippi River near New Orleans.

title: Reconstructed
haiku:
Rust in the old main
a hundred fifty years dark—
Mississippi flows
headline: Democrat Scott Colom won Mississippi's Senate election, becoming the state's first Black senator since Reconstruction.

title: Legwork
haiku:
A boy's new footsteps
machined by strangers' money
the world, briefly, worked
headline: A Sudanese boy who lost his legs in the war received prosthetic limbs after a BBC report sparked a public appeal, and footballer Vinícius Jr. sent him a message of encouragement.

title: Flexural
haiku:
Bridges must bend some
or they shatter. In the Gulf,
two armies, talking.
headline: U.S.-mediated talks on ending the Russia-Ukraine war resumed in Abu Dhabi, with officials saying both sides showed some flexibility.

title: Trickle
haiku:
They keep promising
water will run uphill soon—
a pope says it won't
headline: Pope Leo, visiting Argentina, rebuked President Milei's austerity program and said the economy must serve the needy.

title: Addressable
haiku:
Ten thousand new doors
that lock from the inside now—
bridges back to bridge
headline: Homelessness in the United States fell by its largest margin in more than a decade last year.

title: Mainline
haiku:
Ballots fill the main
the old mains still carry hope
I've seen this before
headline: Control of the U.S. Congress is decided today as midterm elections take place nationwide.

title: Backflow
haiku:
A valve holds the line
no sewage of threats may flow
to poll workers' doors
headline: A federal judge ordered the Trump administration to stop threatening U.S. election officials.

title: Overdrawn
haiku:
They signed for the trees
a bright new line, no pump yet
still, pipes get laid first
headline: Nations reached a global deal to protect nature, though the funding to pay for it remains unresolved.

title: Undammed
haiku:
River keeps its course
votes outrun the chainsaw's roar
I let out my breath
headline: Brazil's Lula won re-election, a result hailed by observers as a win for democracy and the planet.

title: Backflow
haiku:
A judge finds the clog
where slander pooled, now drained clean
the pipe runs true still
headline: A British court found far-right activist Tommy Robinson guilty of harassing two journalists.

title: Runoff
haiku:
Ballots like rainfall
gathering toward the wide drain
a nation still flows
headline: Brazilians voted in a tense presidential runoff between Lula and Bolsonaro's son after massive rallies on the eve of the election.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Votes find a level
Someone wants to dam the count
water keeps its say
headline: The Justice Department is suing to block certification of Alaska's Senate election results if the Republican candidate loses.

title: Clearance
haiku:
I built filters once
now blood learns the trick itself
and tumors drain clean
headline: A personalized skin cancer vaccine significantly cut the risk of the disease returning in a major clinical trial.

title: Pollination
haiku:
No king, they chanted
ballots gather like good rain
the old pipes still hold
headline: Nationwide 'No Kings' Day protests turned their focus toward voter turnout ahead of the midterms.

title: Vacancy
haiku:
Four small chairs, empty
the long hallway holds its breath
Bend, I weep with you
headline: A teenage gunman killed four children, ages 5, 8, and 11, at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, before being shot by a bystander.

title: Succession
haiku:
Diesel deal unwinds —
he says get a new leader
I've seen this excuse
headline: Trump said it may be time for Ukraine to get a new president after Zelensky condemned a diesel deal.

title: Pillar
haiku:
Unseen, the main holds
a jurist, patient as pipe,
wins the prize at last
headline: ICJ judge Navi Pillay was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for her decades of work promoting international law and human rights.

title: Undercurrent
haiku:
Wires we never see
carry feeling cell to cell
old plumber nods, pleased
headline: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded for discoveries showing how nerve cells shape human feelings.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Streets fill like a drain
backed up rent they can't afford
Madrid finds its voice
headline: Tens of thousands of people took to the streets across Spain to protest the country's housing crisis.

title: Wintering
haiku:
Pipes I used to teach
now the target of a war
may God keep them warm
headline: Russia is preparing its most powerful strike yet on Ukraine's energy grid to freeze the country through winter.

title: Outflow
haiku:
Twenty-three years drain
the last convoy leaves Iraq
pipes we built remain
headline: After 23 years, the last American forces have withdrawn from Iraq, leaving the country's future uncertain.

title: Backflow
haiku:
I've heard threats like these
yet the line still carries talk
old pipes, still some flow
headline: Trump threatened Iran with annihilation at the UN, yet the US and Iran held their first talks since June that same week.

title: Pooled
haiku:
I've seen valves shut tight
the press still sues to keep flow
old pipes find daylight
headline: CNN, MS NOW, and Politico are suing the Trump administration after being denied White House press access.

title: Relief
haiku:
One valve turned by hand
Seoul says no more troops abroad
pressure finds its ease
headline: South Korea's president rejected Trump's request to send troops against Iran, choosing restraint over escalation.

title: Confluence
haiku:
Ballots where guns were
a channel dug through old war,
water finds its course
headline: Voters turned out for a landmark election in the Philippines' Muslim autonomous Bangsamoro region, a milestone in the decades-long peace process ending a separatist insurgency.

title: Backflow
haiku:
A valve held its line
someone tried to brew plague code
and the pipe held fast
headline: Anthropic disclosed that it detected and blocked a likely attempt to use its AI models to help develop biological weapons.

title: Crudeness
haiku:
Oil pressure red-lines
old pipes groan toward war again—
I've patched worse than this
headline: Iran signaled readiness to escalate conflict with the U.S. as oil surged past $100 a barrel amid intensifying Middle East turmoil.

title: Undammed
haiku:
Born here, still it flows
a judge holds the old pipe true
bedrock outlasts men
headline: A federal judge blocked the Trump administration's second attempt to restrict birthright citizenship.

title: Waterline
haiku:
Nepal's rivers rose
and swallowed a sleeping town
I have seen this rise
headline: Nepal's flash floods swept away a town, rescuers pulled survivors from a hydropower tunnel, and officials warned a glacial lake could breach and flood again.

title: Spillway
haiku:
A slope gave its ice
the valley drank what no pipe
could ever carry
headline: A collapsed glacier triggered catastrophic flooding across Nepal and Tibet, leaving over 1,500 people missing.

title: Clearance
haiku:
Small lungs, once clogged pipes,
we scrubbed the air and they cleared
I've seen pipes heal too.
headline: A study found children's lung function recovered faster than scientists expected after London's ultra-low emission zone cut air pollution.

title: Unclogged
haiku:
Nine months in shadow
one American walks free
the pipe runs clear now
headline: An American missionary held captive in Niger for nine months has been freed.

title: Reflow
haiku:
Nine months in the pipe
the blockage clears, he walks out
water finds its way
headline: An American missionary kidnapped in Niger was freed after nine months in captivity.

title: Aftershock
haiku:
Ground gave no warning
and swallowed a hundred homes
I light one candle
headline: A powerful earthquake struck western Colombia, killing well over a hundred people as rescuers search the rubble for survivors.

title: Foundation
haiku:
The ground stopped holding
and the roofs came down like rain
we dig by hand now
headline: A major earthquake struck western Colombia, killing more than 130 people and leveling homes.

title: Backflow
haiku:
One valve did not break
though the current pushed, it held
clean water still flows
headline: The Senate let Trump's push for a new voting bill quietly die rather than pass it.

title: Opener
haiku:
Women take the field
history swings open wide
a door long rusted
headline: The Women's Professional Baseball League made its historic debut.

title: Untapped
haiku:
Guns to go silent
one valve turned—not yet the flow
I've seen dry pipes lie
headline: Hamas has agreed to disarm under a Trump-announced Board of Peace plan for Gaza, a tentative but potentially historic first step toward ending the war.

title: Spillover
haiku:
Old pipes want one crack
to spread beyond one border
I have watched this flood
headline: U.S. and Saudi airstrikes on Iran-backed militias have widened the conflict, drawing in Jordan and other regional players.

title: Grapeshot
haiku:
Crews cut a firebreak
as heat leans on Bordeaux vines
I know that thirst well
headline: Wildfires are closing in on Madrid and Bordeaux's vineyards as firefighters in France and Spain race to contain them before an incoming heat wave.

title: Throttled
haiku:
Two days, no new strike
some valve somewhere holds the line
and the crude runs calm
headline: The U.S. and Iran held off on strikes for a second straight day, and oil prices fell on the de-escalation.

title: Sluice
haiku:
Enough hands, one valve
turns, the old minister steps
down, current flows on
headline: India's education minister resigned, handing a win to student protesters who had organized against him.

title: Seepage
haiku:
Signal finds the crack
young hands raise their phones like pipes
truth still finds its grade
headline: Young protesters in India used smartphones to route around Modi government media controls and organize demonstrations.

title: Enrichment
haiku:
Sand traded for glow
another pipe laid toward light
I have capped worse leaks
headline: The U.S. signed a nuclear energy deal with Saudi Arabia, stoking fears of a regional nuclear arms race.

title: Grounded
haiku:
Target the water
and the bridge that lifts the light
the grid always mends
headline: Trump threatened to strike Iran's bridges and power plants if attacks near the Strait of Hormuz continue.

title: Asymmetrical

title: Structural
haiku:
I taught men to build
bridges, pipelines, waterworks —
how quickly boys break
headline: Iran and US widen attacks as renewed conflict shows no sign of de-escalating

title: Sweepingly
haiku:
the sweepers come out
as they did in every war —
brooms outlast bombers
headline: Kyiv hit again as Ukraine reports two dead in Russian strike

title: Half-Mast
haiku:
I outlive them all —
men I argued with for years
the flag still half-mast
headline: Lindsey Graham, longtime South Carolina senator, dies at 71

title: Motherless
haiku:
drones don't have mothers —
that's the engineering point —
someone's son still does
headline: US, Iran launch more attacks as mediators urge both sides to uphold MoU

title: Photogenic
haiku:
the summit's group shot:
smiles rowed up like clean fenceposts
smoke behind the lens
headline: US, Iran threaten more attacks as strikes continue, Trump attends NATO summit

title: Mortality
haiku:
I've buried strongmen
from my armchair, one by one —
the crowds weep; time won't
headline: Mourners throng funeral procession for Iran's supreme leader

title: Remembrance
haiku:
each name read aloud —
no nation is too broken
to remember well
headline: Venezuela quake death toll rises to 3,342 as families search for the missing

title: Anniversary
haiku:
two hundred fifty —
the oath still means what it says
even when we don't
headline: Nation celebrates 250th anniversary of American independence

title: Meteorology
haiku:
"progress," someone says —
a word I trust like weather
still, I check the sky
headline: US-Iran talks in Doha make 'positive progress,' Qatar says

title: Applause
haiku:
five days under stone
and the street still claps for one —
that's the whole species
headline: Venezuela earthquake death toll passes 1,700 as miraculous rescues offer hope

title: Circularity
haiku:
tit, then tat, then tit —
I flunked students for logic
looped as bad as this
headline: US strikes Iranian military sites after tanker attack; Iran retaliates

title: Viticulture
haiku:
forty-four degrees —
the old vines have seen empires
never such a sun
headline: France records hottest day ever at 44.3C amid European heatwave

title: Gracefully
haiku:
he resigns, and goes —
power handed over like
a borrowed garden
headline: Keir Starmer announces resignation as UK prime minister

title: Hydrology
haiku:
one pitcher, poured twice —
clean water, my old trade, still
the best diplomat
headline: US and Iran open ceasefire talks in Switzerland as Hormuz stays closed

title: Endurance
haiku:
thirty-two names read —
the olive trees keep standing
as we keep falling
headline: Israeli airstrikes kill at least 32 in southern Lebanon

title: Reparable
haiku:
the strait opens wide —
gulls escort the tankers home
see? we can fix things
headline: Iran and US sign accord; Strait of Hormuz to reopen as blockades end

title: Grain
haiku:
a grain of dark sky
held ten thousand galaxies—
farther than we dreamed
headline: The James Webb telescope returns its first deep-field images

title: Encore
haiku:
in a locked-down year,
we still reached the rusted plains,
hope wearing a mask
headline: NASA's Perseverance rover lands on Mars

title: Surfacing
haiku:
flood waters rising—
divers thread the flooded dark,
twelve boys breathe again
headline: Twelve boys and their coach are rescued from a flooded Thai cave

title: Comeback
haiku:
nine years through the dark,
to knock on a frozen door,
the dwarf planet smiled
headline: New Horizons makes humanity's first close flyby of Pluto

title: Wedlock
haiku:
the court read the words—
love need not ask permission
now, the rings went on
headline: The U.S. Supreme Court affirms marriage equality nationwide

title: Skycrane
haiku:
seven minutes, dark,
cables lowered a robot,
Mars held its red breath
headline: NASA's Curiosity rover lands safely on Mars

title: Ballast
haiku:
deep beneath the Alps,
a shy field gave the world its
weight—we clapped like fools
headline: Physicists at CERN announce the discovery of the Higgs boson

title: Resurface
haiku:
sixty-nine days dark—
one by one the capsule climbs,
Chile holds its breath
headline: All 33 Chilean miners are rescued alive after 69 days underground

title: Manual
haiku:
we spelled out the book
three billion letters counted—
ourselves, in plain text
headline: The Human Genome Project is completed

title: Keel
haiku:
a can in the black
becomes the first bolted room—
where no nation ends

title: Airbag
haiku:
wrapped in airbags, it
bounced across the rusted sand,
America's Mars

title: Bodyguard
haiku:
a comet shatters—
Jupiter takes the punches
so the earth does not

title: Freeman
haiku:
the long walk was done
he took the oath as free man
a nation stood tall

title: Handshake
haiku:
two shores, one long grudge—
a train now slides beneath waves,
England meets France now
headline: The Channel Tunnel opens, linking Britain and France

title: Farsight
haiku:
we built an eye and
flung it past the atmosphere,
to watch time unfold
headline: The Hubble Space Telescope is launched into orbit

title: Broadcast
haiku:
two stages, one world,
the whole planet passed a hat,
and we all watched close
headline: Live Aid unites the world in a concert for famine relief

title: Longshot
haiku:
twenty kids on skates,
stood up to the biggest team,
and time ran out first

title: Kindling
haiku:
a wish in glass dish
grew into a girl who cried—
time—and she woke thin

title: Mixtape
haiku:
we pressed our whole world
onto gold, and let it fly,
past the edge of home

title: Kin
haiku:
bones in the dry wash
the radio sang her name
grandmother, hello

title: Overflow
haiku:
the fences came down,
half a million found the same
chord in the same rain

title: Overview
haiku:
we watched in gray light,
a man stepped onto the moon—
the whole earth held still

title: Overhead
haiku:
cold wind, borrowed amps,
London looked up from its lunch,
the roof was the stage

title: Borrowed
haiku:
a stranger's engine
stitched into a dying chest—
and dawn, it still beat

title: Alarm
haiku:
a beach-ball of steel
beeped once round the sleeping earth—
and nobody slept

title: Opening
haiku:
the paint wasn't dry,
still, children ran through a dream,
the gates stayed open

haiku:
the summers of fear—
a needle ends the long dread,
children swim again

title: Kinship
haiku:
two brothers, one blood,
a kidney passed like a gift—
no war in the flesh

title: Unlocked
haiku:
they said the wall stood,
one thin man ran through the myth,
and it fell behind

title: Roof
haiku:
two men cut the last
few steps to the roof of earth—
and stood in thin air

title: Spiral
haiku:
two strands climbed and twined,
the code of us laid bare in
one photograph's light

title: Switch
haiku:
three men in a lab
coaxed a crystal to say yes—
the glass tube grew old

title: Skyfloor
haiku:
hard times, hungry streets—
still we raised a spire of steel,
the sky gained a floor

title: Bloom
haiku:
a moldy dish, left
by pure accident, on this—
death lost its footing

title: Solo
haiku:
one man, one thin plane
crossed an ocean, wide awake—
Paris met the dawn

title: Wonders
haiku:
a candle, a crack
gold glinted back through the dust
he breathed: wonders, yes

title: Ballot
haiku:
one state, then the vote—
the ballot box learned her name,
a signature, cast

title: Curvature
haiku:
the sun bent starlight,
and a patent clerk's wild guess
became the whole sky

title: Crossing
haiku:
three faint dots crossed sea
no ship, no wire, only air—
the ocean got small

title: Radiant
haiku:
she boiled tons of ore
to find a pinch that glowed blue—
night forgot to fall

title: Seethrough
haiku:
a strange light passed through
his wife's hand bloomed into bone—
the ring outlived skin
headline: Wilhelm Roentgen discovers X-rays

title: Sugarplum
haiku:
a toy soldier wakes,
snow falls, sugarplums take flight,
and mice learn to dance

title: Overstay
haiku:
a stunt, they all said—
iron lace against gray sky,
it forgot to fall

title: Click
haiku:
you press the button
the rest, he said, is our job
now the moment stays

title: Reprieve
haiku:
a boy, dog-bitten,
fourteen shots against the dark—
the boy did not turn
headline: Louis Pasteur successfully tests his rabies vaccine

title: Echo
haiku:
a needle traced tin
and gave the man his own voice
back to his own ear
headline: Edison announces the phonograph, recording sound for the first time

title: Spike
haiku:
two rails reached for hands
a golden spike rang them shut
the coasts shook hands, done

title: Unshackled
haiku:
December frost bites—
last chains hit the courthouse floor—
free, at last, by law

title: Freehand
haiku:
the new year turned once—
a signature broke the chains,
men woke up as men

title: Cousins
haiku:
all creatures, it turns
share one long and branching root—
we're kin to the moss

title: Pencil
haiku:
they aimed a pencil
at one dark spot in the sky—
and found a planet

title: Key
haiku:
a slab in the mud
held three tongues saying one thing
the silence spoke back

title: Entourage
haiku:
four small lights in line
swung round Jupiter each night—
the earth lost its throne
